rationale: RFC_013 was RATIFIED by the owner on 2026-08-05 on its §2.1 question: per-category provocations ship as ONE FEED FILE PER CATEGORY, not as a keyed map inside the existing `today` object. This submission is the publisher half of that ruling — the half this lane owns. The `tools-api` half (teaching the engine which category a round is for) is NOT in this change and is not ours; it belongs to the gauntlet_dead_cta lane and RFC_013 §2.2 leaves it open. The reason the ruling went this way is a measured property of the reader, not a preference: the Gauntlet engine validates the feed's `today` key for PRESENCE ONLY — three checks in FetchProvocation and no more — then returns it as opaque json.RawMessage, stores those bytes in a jsonb column, and interpolates them straight into the AI prompt. So a keyed-map shape change would have passed every check and been served, silently, as a degraded round. One file per category cannot fail that way: a missing file is a 404, which the existing code already turns into an error and a 503 that the front end handles as its documented degraded mode. The change is deliberately INERT on arrival: every existing row is category 'general', 'general' keeps publishing provocations.json for ever, and migration 283's live schedule row parses unchanged. Nothing observable moves until somebody seeds a second category.

plan.summary: Publisher-side per-category provocations, under a ratified RFC. Category selects the pool rows AND derives the artefact filename; a config whose filename contradicts its category is refused rather than allowed to win; a 404 on the served feed permits a first publish ONLY when the built archive is empty; the daily-uniqueness index moves from (domain, publish_on) to (domain, category, publish_on).

edits.rationale: The filename is DERIVED from the category and a contradicting config is a hard error. This is the edit I most want challenged, because the alternative (let an explicit filename win, as it does today) has a silent and severe failure: migration 283's live schedule row passes `filename: provocations.json` explicitly, so the obvious way to add a category — copy that row — would publish pets' provocation OVER the general feed, which the engine then serves as everybody's daily question. Nothing downstream detects it: the engine never reads a category, and the shrink guard compares archives that are unrelated. Accepting the value when it MATCHES keeps every existing row working, so this refuses contradiction, not redundancy. parseProvocationFeedConfig gains an error return for this and for category validation (the category reaches both a filename and a URL path segment, so it is constrained to 1-40 chars of [a-z0-9-]).

Selection is now per (domain, category). One line of SQL; the archive follows automatically because selectForDate operates on whatever the query returned, so each category gets its own today and its own archive with no further change.
edits.sketch:
func loadProvocations(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, domain, category string) ([]provocation, error) {
    rows, err := db.QueryContext(ctx, `... WHERE domain = $1 AND category = $2 AND status = 'approved' AND publish_on IS NOT NULL ORDER BY publish_on ASC`, domain, category)

edits.rationale: A brand-new category has no artefact, so fetchServedFeed 404s and today's fail-closed rule would make its FIRST publish impossible for ever — the guard forbidding the one case it has nothing to protect. So a 404 now permits the publish, but ONLY when the built feed's archive is empty, which is what a genuine first day looks like. The narrowing is what stops this being a hole: the live general feed carries 8 archive entries, so a SPURIOUS 404 against an established feed still refuses exactly as before, and a new category seeded with back-dated rows also still refuses and must set allow_unverified_publish deliberately for one run. Every other failure (500, timeout, DNS) is untouched and still fails closed — the distinction is between the artefact saying 'I am not there' and the network declining to say anything. shouldBootstrap is a named function specifically SO THAT IT CAN BE TESTED: inlined it would be reachable only through a real 404 against a real domain, which is exactly the property a fail-open path must not have.

Migration 282 made 'one approved provocation per domain per day' unrepresentable via a partial unique index, deliberately. Under categories that rule is wrong — two categories are separate dailies and must both publish on the same date — but the SHAPE of the protection is right and is kept: uniqueness is still an INDEX, not a check in the publisher, so two approved rows in ONE category on ONE date remain unrepresentable. The new index is created BEFORE the old is dropped so there is no window in which a concurrent insert could create the duplicate the old index forbade. The verify block INDUCES both directions rather than asserting the index exists — two categories on one date must be accepted, a second row in one category must be refused — and is written as DO/RAISE rather than SELECTs because ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result set, so a verify block made of SELECTs cannot stop the COMMIT.

edits.symbol: six new tests + the parseProvocationFeedConfig call sites
edits.rationale: The load-bearing test is TestDefaultCategoryKeepsTheOriginalFilenameForever: the entire safety case for option (a) is that the default artefact is untouched, and if that ever changes every reader breaks at once, engine included. TestAFilenameContradictingItsCategoryIsRefused pins the silent-overwrite failure described above. TestBootstrapIsPermittedOnlyForAGenuineFirstPublish drives the real shouldBootstrap across a five-row table — an earlier draft re-stated the condition inline and therefore could not have failed for ANY edit to the code, which is recorded in the lane NOTES as a caught misstep. It is paired with TestTheBootstrapTableWouldCatchDroppingTheArchiveCondition, a can-fail control asserting that the two variants genuinely disagree on an established feed, so the table is not passing by accident.

grounded_in: internal/tools-api/handlers/round.go:73-80 — the COMPLETE validation of the feed: `today, ok := payload["today"]; if !ok { return nil, fmt.Errorf("fetch provocations: missing 'today' key in response") }` then `if len(today) == 0 || string(today) == "null" { ... }`. Three checks, no fourth. This is why a shape change is undetectable and why the owner ruled for one file per category.

internal/tools-api/handlers/round.go:44 — `func FetchProvocation(domain string) (json.RawMessage, error)`. The value is returned as opaque bytes and never parsed; the only Unmarshal in the path is :70, on the envelope `map[string]json.RawMessage`, to find the key.

internal/tools-api/handlers/position.go:67 and defend.go:67 — `` ` + string(round.Provocation) + ` `` . The raw feed bytes are interpolated directly into the AI prompt, so a wrong shape degrades a round rather than erroring.

internal/tools-api/handlers/round.go:59-61 — `if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK { return nil, fmt.Errorf("fetch provocations: upstream status %d", resp.StatusCode) }`, and :98-107 turns that into a 503 (503 specifically, because Cloudflare replaces a 502's body — bugs_closed/083). This is the LOUD path a missing per-category file takes, and it is the whole argument for option (a).

grep over internal/tools-api/**.go excluding tests — `headline`, `teaser`, `slug`, `detail_body` return ZERO hits. No field of `today` is named anywhere server-side, so nothing there can notice a shape change.

`go list -deps ./platform/orchestration/actions | grep tools-api` → no rows (measured 2026-08-05). The publisher imports nothing from tools-api; the two sides share httpguard and aiservice and no type describing the feed. There is no compile-time check of this contract and there never has been.

docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/283_provocation_feed_publisher.sql:117-124 — the live schedule row's input_data passes `'filename', 'provocations.json'` explicitly. This is the row an operator would copy to add a category, and it is why the filename/category contradiction must be an error rather than an override.

docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/282_provocation_pool.sql:101-103 — `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_provocations_one_per_day ON provocations (domain, publish_on) WHERE publish_on IS NOT NULL AND status = 'approved'`, with the comment 'makes that unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged'. Migration 320 preserves that intent and rescopes it to the unit that actually has one daily.

docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/282_provocation_pool.sql:62 — `category text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'general'`, added early on purpose, with its own comment naming this exact engine constraint. No data migration is implied: live pool is 9 rows, all 'general' (SELECT confirmed 2026-08-05).

live clients_db, 2026-08-05, AFTER applying 320 — SELECT indexname FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename='provocations' → idx_provocations_one_per_category_day, idx_provocations_schedule_by_category, provocations_domain_slug_key, provocations_pkey. The two old indexes are gone and the two new ones exist. The migration's own induced verify (two categories one date accepted; same category twice refused with unique_violation) ran inside the runner's rollback probe before it was applied for real.

live artefact, 2026-08-05 — https://vonc.com/data/provocations.json carries 8 archive entries. That is the number that makes the bootstrap narrowing meaningful: a spurious 404 against the established general feed still refuses, because 8 != 0.

OWNER RULING 2026-08-05, RFC_013 §7 — 'one file per category I think'. §2.2 (who edits tools-api), §2.3 (should a round record its category) and §2.4 (shared Go type) are explicitly NOT ruled and remain open to the gauntlet_dead_cta lane.
plan.risks: (1) THE CHANGE IS INERT ON ARRIVAL and that is the main thing to verify, not that categories work: every pool row is 'general', 'general' derives provocations.json, and mig 283's row parses unchanged — so the next scheduled run must behave EXACTLY as today. The honest verification is a no-change run (committed:false, reason 'no change since the served feed'), not a successful category publish, because there is no second category to publish. (2) THE BOOTSTRAP PATH IS A WIDENING of the default failure behaviour on one branch, and I have named it rather than buried it, because the council caught the REVERSE mistake on this same function once: the first draft published blind on any fetch failure, disabling the shrink guard during exactly the infrastructure trouble most likely to accompany a bad deploy. The narrowing to archive==0 is what I want reviewed hardest. (3) I CANNOT PROVE THE 404 PATH IN PRODUCTION without creating a category, so it is covered by unit tests against the real shouldBootstrap plus a can-fail control, and is UNEXERCISED LIVE. Stated plainly. (4) DEPLOY ASYMMETRY: the migration is live NOW (DB config is immediate) while the Go half is inert until an image rolls. That ordering is safe in this direction and only this direction — the old binary queries without a category filter and is unaffected by the index change, because every row is 'general'. The reverse order would not have been safe. (5) NOT COVERED, DELIBERATELY: tools-api. FetchProvocation still takes a domain only, and provocStore is still keyed by domain alone with a 5-minute TTL — a per-category feed will need a category dimension in that cache key or categories would serve each other's provocations for up to five minutes. That is RFC_013 §2.2, it is the gauntlet lane's code, and it is flagged in their cold-start INCOMING block and as a landmine on round.go. Its absence here is a decision, not an oversight. (6) A SECOND CATEGORY IS NOT SEEDABLE END-TO-END YET for that reason: the publisher would happily write provocations-pets.json, and nothing would read it.
